page: Amazon Web Services c8id.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs operating at a sustained 3.9 GHz clock frequency. The processor incorporates an extensive 480 MB L3 cache alongside hardware support for vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. Memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, delivering a compute-centric ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local ephemeral storage is provided via a direct-attached 1,900 GB NVMe solid-state drive, backed by a 15 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark assessments show strong capabilities in compute-intensive and data manipulation tasks. The instance delivers top-quartile performance in single-core and multi-core Geekbench evaluations, registering scores of 2,205.0 and 18,417.0 respectively, accompanied by top-tier text processing metrics. Compression tests reflect strong throughput, exceeding 34 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 231 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Static web serving throughput reaches 57.59 GB/sec. Small language model inference benefits heavily from the CPU instruction set, achieving top-decile text generation throughput of 371.41 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model. Meanwhile, raw memory bandwidth and synthetic multi-core stress-ng tests perform squarely in the median range.

From an operational and resource-efficiency perspective, the bundled 1,900 GB NVMe SSD eliminates the need to attach separate high-throughput block volumes for temporary files, staging data, or cache layers. However, workloads requiring expansive memory allocations will find the 2 GB per core ratio restrictive compared to general-purpose or memory-optimized alternatives. Amazon Web Services c8id.8xlarge is best suited for compute-heavy batch processing, Clang compilation pipelines, text analytics, lightweight CPU-based inference, and high-concurrency web serving requiring fast local caching.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. It features 64 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding a focused 2 GB per core ratio. Hardware capabilities include a 480 MB L3 cache, advanced instruction support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX, and 15 Gbps baseline networking. Storage demands are supported by a bundled 1,900 GB local NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPU accelerators are present. Benchmarks demonstrate strong performance across multi-core compute, compression, static web serving, and small-model inference workloads. With high single-thread speeds and dense local NVMe storage, this server is suitable for CPU-bound tasks, CI/CD compilation, and high-throughput web infrastructure.
